full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, J: This Rule arises out of an application under Section-15(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioners and directed against the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 dated 31.3.1994 rejecting the application of the petitioners under Sections-151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed for setting aside the abatement order dated 12.9.1988 passed in Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 and to substitute the petitioners in place of their predecessor. 

 2. The short facts of the petitioner's case is that their predecessor Abdur Razzak was tenant under defendant opposite party herein namely Most. Rezia Begum. She was trying to evict the predecessor of the plaintiff petitioners from the suit premises by force without any due process of law as a result he filed Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 for permanent injunction against the aforesaid land lady. That there was a lease agreement in between the landlady and their predecessor Abdur Razzak, In the lease agreement there was a clause that all the terms and conditions of the agreement shall be binding and enforceable against both the parties and their heirs, executors, representatives and assignees and there was another clause in the said agreement that tenant shall be able to sub-let the premises or any portion of it etc. and also it has been further stipulated that the tenant shall be able to erect sheds in the vacant land at his own costs for his business and in paragraph 7 of the petition the petitioner tried to state that after being partitioned the suit premises had fallen in the share of one Khaja, who also subsequently executed another tenancy lease agreement in favour of the predecessor of the petitioners and in that agreement it was categorically stipulated that the tenant or their heirs shall not be asked to vacate the premises in question. 

 6. I have perused I he record and application for revision and heard the learned Advocate for the opposite party who produced the copy of the application filed by the petitioners in the court below under section 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I have also perused the same the ends of justice in which amongst ether grounds it was slated that the order dated 12.9.1988 was mistaken order passed by the trial court and for the ends of justice it is required to be set aside by reviewing the earlier order dated 12.9.1988 and the original Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 required to be restored to its original file and number and also to substitute the petitioners in place of their predecessors. The learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by the impugned order dated 31.3.1994 rejected the petition of the petitioners herein on the ground that the suit was abated due to the death of sole plaintiff by an order dated 12.9.1988 passed by his predecessor and without filing appeal against the said order the present application filed after lapse of 5 years under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable and cannot be allowed. Moreover after the death of the tenant, his heirs cannot be substituted in his place and thus it was rejected.
